FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox project-level analysis. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it copies only the target file into a temp dir as `basename(target_path)`, then runs `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit` on that isolated file path. For multi-file modules, relative imports and same-package references are no longer resolved against the real project layout. A fix can therefore be marked HARMFUL or SAFE based on diagnostics caused by the broken sandbox shape rather than by the patch itself. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no package tree or sibling files are copied; tool runners are then invoked on this lone file.
FOLLOW: This crosses the immune/endocrine interface directly because immune stage 4 uses `from bench.endocrine import evaluate_fixes` to decide whether a finding becomes `verified=True`. False HARMFUL verdicts prevent correct fixes from closing bugs; false SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts can also occur when imports disappear and tool coverage changes. Downstream, NK bug-closed gating and escalation logic depend on `verified`, so mis-evaluation here causes bugs to stay open, churn across rounds, or be escalated incorrectly.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the file within a mirrored project tree instead of as a standalone basename: copy all `source_paths` into a temp directory preserving relative paths, write the patched target at its original relative path, and run tools from the temp project root against that mirrored path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND — optional tests in `evaluate_fix()` are not run against the patched code unless the provided `test_cmd` is already tempdir-aware. The code sets `cwd=tmpdir` but executes the caller’s command unchanged. In the active immune pipeline, `test_cmd=["python3","-m","pytest","bench/tests/","-x","-q","--tb=no","--no-header","-q"]`. The temp dir contains only the patched file, not `bench/tests/`, so pytest from `cwd=tmpdir` cannot find the test tree. If the command uses absolute paths, it may instead test the real source tree, not the sandbox. Either way, “sandbox-test proposed fixes” is not happening reliably.
FOLLOW: This makes the advertised fix-evaluation feature partially dead on the happy path. A fix can be marked SAFE without exercising the patched codebase, or tests can fail for missing test paths unrelated to the fix and mark it HARMFUL. Because immune stage 4 uses these verdicts to set `verified=True`, the bug-closed gate and reviewer-facing status become silently wrong.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when creating the temp sandbox, mirror the project subtree needed by `test_cmd` as well as `source_paths`, then rewrite the test command to target paths inside the sandbox project root before execution.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as another tool’s issue count drops by a larger amount. It sums deltas: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; only `total_net > 0` is HARMFUL, and `total_net < 0` is SAFE. Example from code semantics: `+1` new Bandit issue and `-2` Ruff issues yields `total_net = -1` => SAFE, despite a new security issue introduced.
FOLLOW: This is silently wrong output, not just a quality issue. Immune stage 4 treats SAFE and NEUTRAL as grounds to set `verified=True`, so a fix that regresses type safety or security can be marked programmatically verified and close the bug. NK then suppresses later duplicate reports via the bug-closed gate, causing a real regression to be hidden from subsequent rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — mark the fix HARMFUL if any individual net delta is positive; only mark SAFE when at least one delta is negative and none are positive.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` records zero-based line and column numbers from pyright JSON without converting them to the 1-based convention used by the other tool parsers and by most source diagnostics. Code: `line=rng.get("line", 0)`, `column=rng.get("character", 0)`. Pyright’s JSON `range.start.line` / `character` are zero-based. Ruff, Bandit, and mypy paths here all emit 1-based values.
FOLLOW: The health scan then mixes coordinate systems in a single `HealthScan.diagnostics` stream. Any consumer that displays or correlates diagnostics by line number gets silent off-by-one locations for pyright only. That degrades defect triage and can misattribute issues when reviewers compare endocrine output with source lines or other tool findings.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add 1 to pyright `line` and `character` when populating `ToolDiagnostic`, preserving 0 only when the field is absent.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A mention like `brain.py` will match any source path containing that substring, and a short relative fragment can match multiple files. The function returns the first such path, with no uniqueness check.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` then patches and evaluates the wrong file while still attributing the verdict to `finding.finding_id`. This produces silently wrong SAFE/HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE results, contaminates immune verification, and can set `verified=True` on a finding whose proposed fix was never applied to its real target.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require unambiguous resolution: prefer exact normalized path or basename equality among `source_paths`, and if multiple matches remain, return `None` so the fix is UNEVALUABLE instead of patching the wrong file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` claims to provide tool availability, but even beyond missing-binary cases already registered, it leaves unavailable tools absent from `tools_available` entirely when `existing` is empty and when a runner returns normally with internal parse failure. Returned `HealthScan.tools_available` is therefore not a stable full map of known tools. Evidence: early return on `if not existing`; aggregate loop only inserts keys for the four iterated tools after calling runners; parse failures inside runners still look “available”.
FOLLOW: Consumers cannot distinguish “tool unavailable”, “tool not run”, and “tool ran but parse failed” from the returned structure. That weakens the endocrine-to-brain contract and makes health reporting misleading, especially when reviewer decisions depend on whether static-analysis coverage actually happened.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — always return all expected tool keys with explicit boolean availability, and separately record execution/parsing status if needed; at minimum initialize all four tool names to `False` before scanning and update only on confirmed execution.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0001 | `tools_available` is also incomplete on the empty-source-path path and on parse-failure paths, so the current contract conflates “not run”, “not installed”, and “ran but unparsable”. The fix should initialize explicit status for every tool, not just patch the NOT_FOUND case.

EXTEND C0005 | the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes (no source modification)” is only partially true: analysis is sandboxed, but project structure and tests are not mirrored, so the key feature can misfire on valid multi-file fixes and test commands.
